defects.description: The inner comparison `collection[k] > collection[min_index]` selects the maximum of the remaining elements instead of the minimum, producing a descending sort; it should be `<`.
paraphrases: `>` should be `<`; selection sort must find the minimum, not the maximum.
Tracking the largest element reverses the sort order.
selection_sort([0,5,3,2,2]) would not be ascending with `>`.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `collection[k] < collection[min_index]`. Real (wrong order), findable via the ascending docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The inner scan `range(i + 1, length - 1)` stops one element early, so the last element is never considered when searching for the minimum.
paraphrases: `range(i + 1, length - 1)` should be `range(i + 1, length)`; the last index is skipped.
The inner loop omits the final element from the minimum search.
Off-by-one in the inner range can miss the true minimum.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `range(i + 1, length)`. Real (may miss the minimum), findable via the docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The minimum index is initialised to `0` instead of the current position `i`, so for later passes it can select an already-sorted element and swap it into place, corrupting the result.
paraphrases: `min_index = 0` should be `min_index = i`; the search must start at the current position.
Starting the minimum index at 0 lets already-sorted elements be reselected.
The candidate minimum should be i, not the first element, on every pass.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `min_index = i`. Real (corrupts the sorted prefix), findable by reading the pass logic, distinct.
